snippet.textDisplay: Native to Florida. Dude this game is way too accurate. Love the No wake manatee signs in the ocean, the tolls are called Vice Pass instead of Sun Pass, the weather is astonishingly accurate- the dense clouds in the distance at all times that loom the threat of rain, down to the grassy unkempt sand roads. Dude- even the bridges going over bodies of water- have the same structure. The one thing I have to wait and see is the terrain. Florida is unbelievably flat- so there’s a lot less up and down. I doubt there would be any mountains- but GTA without a mountain just doesn’t sound right.

snippet.textDisplay: I’ve been a scuba diver for 11 years now. Yes there is a lot that goes into learning how to dive. But ultimately it’s a sport of common sense. Rule 1: don’t stop breathing. Rule 2: don’t touch anything you don’t know what it is. Rule 3: know your safety stops/listen to your computer. Part of training is learning to read the equipment without a computer, but so many places use dive computers that tell you everything you need to know anyway. There are a lot of ways you can get hurt, sure, but they’re also largely easy to manage.

snippet.textDisplay: Hey jack, you asked why Lucia would keep pulling back the upper receiver of the firearm during dry fire drills near the end of your video, and I figured I'd answer. Basically, the firearm needs the upper slide to fully cycle back then forward in order to reset the trigger and it won't cycle without the kinetic force of an actual bullet being fired, so she has to manually reset it in order to practice her trigger squeeze.
